questions.question: Which set is the feasible region $F$ of an optimization model?
options: The plans that satisfy every constraint of the model
The plans that satisfy at least one of the constraints
The plans that give the best value of the objective
The plans that satisfy all but the sign conditions

questions.question: A model's objective is changed from making $3x_1+2x_2$ as large as possible to making $x_1-x_2$ as small as possible, with the constraints unchanged. What happens to its feasible region $F$?
options: $F$ shrinks to the plans best for the new aim
$F$ stays exactly the same set of feasible plans
$F$ is reflected, as the aim is now reversed
$F$ changes, since it is built for one objective

questions.question: In a model with two variables, each constraint allows a certain region of the $(x_1,x_2)$-plane. How is the feasible region $F$ formed from these regions?
options: As their union: the points lying in any one region
As the region of the most restrictive constraint
As the lines where constraints hold with equality
As their overlap: the points lying in every region

questions.question: The feasible region $F$ of a model turns out to be empty. What does this mean?
options: Only the plan with every variable equal to 0 is allowed
Plans exist, but none gives a best value of the objective
Every possible plan breaks every one of the constraints
No plan satisfies all of the constraints at the same time

questions.question: A model in $x_1,x_2$ has the constraints $x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. What do the last two constraints do to its feasible region $F$?
options: They keep $F$ in the first quadrant, axes included
Nothing, since sign conditions are not part of $F$
They keep $F$ off the axes, so all plans are positive
They matter only once an objective has been chosen

questions.question: A model has the constraints $x_1+2x_2\le8$, $3x_1+x_2\le9$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which point lies in its feasible region?
A model has the constraints $x_1+x_2=4$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. What does its feasible region look like?
options: The triangle on or below $x_1+x_2=4$ in the first quadrant
The segment of $x_1+x_2=4$ between $(4,0)$ and $(0,4)$
The whole line $x_1+x_2=4$, in both directions
Only the two axis points $(4,0)$ and $(0,4)$

questions.question: The decision variables $x_1$ and $x_2$ must be whole numbers $0,1,2,\dots$, and the only other constraint is $x_1+x_2\le2$. How many points does the feasible region contain?
options: $3$ points
$9$ points
$6$ points
Infinitely many points

questions.question: A model has the constraints $x_1\le3$, $x_2\le2$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which extra constraint could be added without changing the feasible region?
Each system below is combined with $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which system gives an empty feasible region?
One constraint is removed from a model whose feasible region is $F$; the new feasible region is $F'$. Which statement must hold?
options: $F'$ is part of $F$, since a constraint is gone
$F'$ contains all of $F$ and maybe more plans
$F'$ is always strictly larger than $F$
$F'$ may gain some plans and lose others

questions.question: How is a feasible solution $\boldsymbol{x}$ of a model related to the feasible region $F$ of the same model?
options: $F$ is the feasible solution with the best objective value
$\boldsymbol{x}$ is feasible only if it lies on the edge of $F$
$\boldsymbol{x}$ is feasible exactly when it is a point of $F$
$F$ collects feasible solutions only once an objective is set

questions.question: A plan $\boldsymbol{x}$ does not belong to the feasible region $F$ of a model. Which statement about $\boldsymbol{x}$ must be true?
options: $\boldsymbol{x}$ breaks every constraint of the model
$\boldsymbol{x}$ breaks at least one model constraint
$\boldsymbol{x}$ breaks one of the sign conditions
$\boldsymbol{x}$ lies on one of the constraint lines

questions.question: Each system below is combined with $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which one gives a feasible region that extends without limit?
A model has the constraints $x_1+x_2=4$, $x_1\le1$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which set is its feasible region?
options: $\{(t,4-t)\colon 0\le t\le4\}$
$\{(t,4-t)\colon 0\le t\le1\}$
$\{(t,4-t)\colon 1\le t\le4\}$

questions.question: In the $(x_1,x_2)$-plane, a feasible region consists of the first-quadrant points on or below the line through $(6,0)$ and $(0,3)$. Which constraint, together with $x_1,x_2\ge0$, describes it?
Every constraint of a model, taken on its own, is satisfied by some plan. What follows for the feasible region $F$?
options: $F$ is non-empty, since every constraint can be met
$F$ contains each plan that meets one of the constraints
$F$ is non-empty whenever there are just two constraints
$F$ may still be empty, since constraints can conflict

questions.question: The feasible region $F$ of a model in which the objective is to be made as small as possible extends without limit. Can the objective then be made as small as one likes?
options: Not necessarily; a smallest value may still exist
Yes; plans far out make the objective arbitrarily small
No; such a region always has a smallest objective value
Yes, for every objective that is not constant

questions.question: A model has the constraints $x_1+x_2\ge2$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$, so its feasible region extends without limit. Which objective has a smallest value over this region, with that value correctly stated?

Variables $x_1,x_2$ count whole crates of 4 tonnes, so $x_1,x_2\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, and a lorry must carry at least 6 and at most 7 tonnes: $4x_1+4x_2\ge6$ and $4x_1+4x_2\le7$. Which statement about the feasible region $F$ is correct?
options: $F$ contains $(1.5,0)$, which meets both load constraints
$F$ contains $(1,1)$, found by rounding $x_1+x_2$ up to 2
$F$ contains $(1,0)$, found by rounding $x_1+x_2$ down to 1
$F$ is empty: no whole sum $x_1+x_2$ lies in $[1.5,\ 1.75]$
